shoal_e14_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_entry.text: On Day Three Hundred Twenty-Two, the leg-injured worker asked Yue to use his name when speaking to him. Tian Bo, he said, was easier to hear than the fourth rescued man. His partner introduced herself as Shao Jin. They had offered Yue a short visit after her paid receiving shift, not a public account of their entire household. Bo's leg lay supported under the ordinary practitioner's current plan. Rescue had brought him out of the shed. His days now had to fit a body that could not work as before.

shoal_e14_care_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_01.text: Bo's first accepted rehabilitation session cost four copper from the reserved forty-copper line. The qualified practitioner worked on the permitted early motion and explained what remained prohibited. It was not a test of whether Bo wanted recovery enough. Pain and current bone condition had actual limits. Yue watched only the part Bo offered, from the public side of the room, and supplied neither qi nor an opinion that the exercise ought to look more heroic.

shoal_e14_care_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_02.text: Jin had brought Bo's current questions in her own small notebook. She asked how far a seated rest could last before his leg needed a different position, what signs required earlier return, and who should be contacted if an appointment moved. The practitioner answered within his actual current assessment. He did not hand her a guarantee of a perfect leg. She copied the useful instructions and kept asking until the ordinary words matched the life they had to arrange.

shoal_e14_care_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_03.text: The initial four employees' care scopes had actually been performed and received, eight copper each, thirty-two in all. The provider's record kept their private clinical details with the proper patients. Six copper of the dressings line had supplied the actual earlier materials under its accepted scope. Further rehabilitation, travel, income support, and later dressing work remained future or current separate entries. One hundred twenty reserved did not mean one hundred twenty had already been spent.

shoal_e14_care_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_04.text: On Day Three Hundred Twenty-Three, the accepted brace was fitted under qualified ordinary supervision for eight copper from the rehabilitation-and-support line. The clinic's temporary splint returned to its proper custodian. Bo owned the accepted brace under its actual receiving terms. It did not give him permission to haul a crate. He disliked how conspicuous it was, then asked whether a trouser seam could be altered so it caught less often.

shoal_e14_care_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_05.text: Jin chose an ordinary mender under her own small accepted payment for the garment change, outside the care deposit's specified brace cost. Yue did not volunteer to use energy on cloth because she wanted the couple spared another errand. The mender asked Bo how he actually dressed and made a removable opening suited to the brace. An ordinary adaptation could support care without being the same thing as clinical recovery.

shoal_e14_care_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_06.text: The first five-copper restricted-income payment was actually received on Day Three Hundred Twenty-Three. It came from the care deposit's finite thirty-copper line, one of six weekly payments. It was support, not a full replacement of Bo's lost trade income or payment for a new job he had not accepted. Jin had her own net-repair work. They would still need to decide what ordinary household costs and later work they could sustain.

shoal_e14_care_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_07.text: Bo said people kept saying at least he had survived, as though the phrase settled everything after breath. He was grateful for the crew and angry at his leg, his damaged shop, and the sound of the word lucky. Yue told him about the cup's bad foot instead of claiming her bruise matched his fracture. He laughed, then asked whether the potter had charged her for the joke. The conversation gave him room to be a person between care instructions.

shoal_e14_care_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_08.text: Jin asked whether Yue's small-talisman task could help the brace fit. Yue said it was qualified only for its local marker setup and no medical or brace application. The current ordinary practitioner and fitter had the relevant skills. Jin accepted the answer without calling it disappointing. She wanted to know what was actually available, not another hopeful suggestion that would leave her asking strangers whether a remedy existed behind their polite refusal.

shoal_e14_care_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_09.text: On the same afternoon, the public care-logistics desk offered an auxiliary two-hour receiving interval after Yue's assigned shift. Two consenting families needed to check current journey bookings before their deadlines. The staffed desk could manage its existing load, but the extra interval needed a willing trained receiving helper. Yue's current job experience qualified the ordinary receiving scope. It would not authorize her to decide clinical plans or guarantee that a carrier had traveled before its actual day.

shoal_e14_care_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_10.text: Bo separately asked whether she would sit with him for two offered hours while Jin completed an ordinary net-repair appointment. He wanted company, not a medical attendant. His current plan required no new treatment during that interval, and qualified staff remained reachable through their actual roles. Jin's repair was an existing client's offered four-copper task, payable after completion. She had not accepted it yet because she wanted Bo's preference and the companion arrangement clear.

shoal_e14_care_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_11.text: The desk interval and the companion visit overlapped. Other suitable helpers had not accepted those particular hours, and the offer would not become fully staffed by saying somebody must care. If Yue took the private visit, Jin could choose to accept the paid repair while Bo had requested company. If Yue took the public desk, Jin could stay with Bo and decline that four-copper opportunity. The two other families would seek later receiving if the auxiliary desk did not open now.

shoal_e14_care_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_12.text: Yue asked the desk what a missed interval would mean. The two families had valid existing claims and care plans; neither would lose treatment rights. Their current carrier booking deadlines would pass, and later travel dates would need new accepted arrangements. Their care accounts were separate from Bo's one-hundred-twenty-copper deposit. She asked Bo what the visit meant to him. He said he was tired of speaking only to people who asked where it hurt.

shoal_e14_care_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_13.text: The choice did not belong to who deserved care. Both offered roles were ordinary unpaid assistance after Yue's four paid hours, within a body currently cleared for such sitting and walking. She could decline either or accept one finite interval, with no indefinite obligation created by it. The other people kept their own choices and processes. Yue wanted to do one because it was useful and because she had time, not because a certificate made every gap hers.

shoal_e14_care_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_14.text: Jin's net client needed an answer before the afternoon tide because its own boat repair depended on the ties. The care desk needed its helper before the two families arrived. Bo had asked for company and accepted that Yue might choose the other role. His consent did not bind Jin to go; hers did not bind Yue to sit. The offers were concrete enough that a refusal could be respected and a completed hour could be named afterward.

shoal_e14_care_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_care_15.text: Yue kept her current clinical limits in mind while answering. She would not lift Bo, administer a treatment, or carry a family's heavy bags. The actual help could be a conversation with an offered private person or orderly receiving at a public table. One path would let a partner earn four copper and a patient hear something besides care. The other could keep two families' current booked roads available. She chose the hour she wished to fulfill.

shoal_e14_help_choice.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_help_choice.text: After her paid shift, Yue had one two-hour interval. Bo asked for ordinary company so Jin could choose the offered four-copper net repair. The public desk asked for a trained receiving helper so two consenting families could confirm current care journeys before booking deadlines. Existing care remained staffed and rights intact. These were different people's real hours. Yue chose which finite offer to accept.

choices.text: Sit with Bo while Jin completes the offered repair.
Staff the auxiliary public receiving desk for the two families.

shoal_e14_companion_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_companion_01.text: Jin took the net appointment after Bo confirmed that he wanted the offered company. She left a pot of ordinary tea within easy reach and told him when she expected to return. Yue sat beside the window, leaving the brace and his supported leg alone. Outside, someone was chasing a chicken between empty packing baskets. Bo watched the pursuit with an interest no rehabilitation exercise had managed to earn that morning.

shoal_e14_companion_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_companion_02.text: The chicken escaped onto the public lane. Its pursuer stopped at the carts instead of charging into a moving axle, then began bargaining with a fish seller whose stall it had adopted. Bo had once owned a hen that stole chalk. He described finding white marks across his workshop floor and accusing an apprentice before noticing the bird's guilty beak. Yue laughed hard enough that her own elbow reminded her to sit differently.

shoal_e14_companion_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_companion_03.text: Bo asked about her first paid work. Yue told him about the indignity of receiving instructions from someone younger who nevertheless knew the work better. He approved of that younger person immediately. A workshop, he said, could survive an ignorant newcomer if the newcomer learned. It could not survive a newcomer who treated correction as an insult. He missed being irritated by apprentices over small mistakes that could actually be repaired.

shoal_e14_companion_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_companion_04.text: He did not want to sell his shop now. He might later, but he disliked visitors deciding that a damaged leg meant a different occupation had already been chosen. Yue asked which ordinary work he could imagine doing seated when his practitioner permitted it. He named estimating small repairs, teaching a willing apprentice to sort fastenings, and telling customers which proposed repairs were foolish. The last task, he thought, needed very little walking.

shoal_e14_companion_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_companion_05.text: A bell from the clinic interrupted him. Neither mistook it for a summons to every patient. Bo knew his own appointment and current instructions. He asked Yue to open the window another finger's width because the room smelled of boiled linen. She moved the latch without reaching over him. Fresh harbor air brought salt, hot bread, and the disagreeable sweetness of a rubbish cart overdue for its collection.

shoal_e14_companion_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_companion_06.text: At the public desk, the auxiliary receiving hours remained unopened. Its assigned staff completed their existing patients' work. The two families arrived with papers that still needed individual checking and could not be fitted into those already committed hours. Their present carrier deadlines passed. They retained their care plans and could arrange later journeys, but this week's available seats were not saved for them by another person's private visit.

shoal_e14_companion_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_companion_07.text: Yue learned that consequence when a desk messenger passed the window on his ordinary round. He gave no patient names or clinical details. The families would receive new booking dates after the current carriers closed their lists. Bo heard enough to understand why Yue might have chosen differently. He did not thank her by declaring those families less important. He said only that he was glad she had come.

shoal_e14_companion_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_companion_08.text: The conversation turned to the harbor's old fire. Bo had been a child when one burned a western warehouse, and the first thing he remembered was an adult making him carry somebody else's angry cat. The adults later argued over the building. He remembered the cat. He wondered which ordinary absurdity a child might carry from this fire, something the town's official speeches would never think to preserve.

shoal_e14_companion_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_companion_09.text: Yue described the school drawing that had put her inside a place she had never entered. Bo considered it, then asked whether the revised drawing still allowed the child to make something beautiful. She said the child had separated imagined art from an alarm diagram checked against actual witnesses. Bo nodded. A truthful diagram could be ugly. A picture could imagine. The harm came when people forgot which one they were using.

shoal_e14_companion_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_companion_10.text: Jin returned with four copper received for the completed repair. The client's net ties had passed its ordinary pull check, and the client had accepted the work. She laid the coins beside her own notebook rather than folding them into Bo's care deposit. She was pleased, then tired, then annoyed that the room's tea had gone cold. All three feelings survived being grateful that the offered arrangement had worked.

shoal_e14_companion_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_companion_11.text: Yue left when the two hours ended. Jin chose to sit with Bo afterward, and neither asked Yue to make tomorrow another promise. On the lane, she passed the shuttered auxiliary table and saw two families' later-booking notices being prepared. Her useful afternoon had left a real gap elsewhere. She could own the choice without inventing an answer that would make every person equally glad she had made it.

shoal_e14_companion_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_companion_12.text: That evening Jin showed Bo the repaired net's payment in her household figures. Four copper could buy useful food and still fail to replace a lost trade. Bo asked whether she wanted him to praise her for keeping everything together. She said she wanted him to ask how the client had treated her. He did. The question changed the evening more than the coins, and Yue was absent from that conversation.

shoal_e14_public_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_public_01.text: Yue accepted the auxiliary desk's two hours. Jin declined the client's current four-copper repair offer and stayed with Bo by her own choice. The client hired someone else before the tide turned. Nothing in Bo's existing qualified care depended on Yue opening the public table. Jin would not receive payment for a repair she had not performed, and the missed work would not be quietly added to a later household total.

shoal_e14_public_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_public_02.text: The first family arrived with a journey form folded so often that its printed date had nearly separated from the page. Yue flattened it under a clean ordinary weight and asked the consenting adult to identify the current booking. He had a valid care plan, but an earlier address remained on the carrier's copy. She could receive and correct the supplied contact information. She could not decide that a previous journey had happened.

shoal_e14_public_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_public_03.text: The adult's daughter held their basket and watched the doorway. She was old enough to dislike being spoken over and young enough that every clerk seemed taller when seated. Yue asked which contact she wanted used for messages sent to her. The daughter gave her own preferred ordinary receiving address. Her father's answer did not replace hers. It took another minute and saved the carrier from sending a notice to a household that had moved.

shoal_e14_public_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_public_04.text: The carrier's actual receiving clerk checked the corrected request against available seats and accepted the booking before its deadline. Yue witnessed that ordinary step and returned the family's original papers. The journey itself remained on its proper future date. The adult asked whether this meant his practitioner would find him better. Yue said it meant the carrier had accepted their current transport arrangement. He laughed at himself, then looked relieved anyway.

shoal_e14_public_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_public_05.text: The second family had brought the wrong copy of a payment record. It showed an earlier deposit, not the current journey allocation. Yue explained the difference without calling them careless. A consenting relative could reach the nearby receiving office before it closed. She kept their place at the auxiliary table while that person fetched the actual current extract. The first family's work had not made the second family's separate account magically match.

shoal_e14_public_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_public_06.text: While they waited, the older woman described her first sea crossing. She had spent it furious with a gull that kept landing on the rail as though the boat belonged to it. Yue asked whether the gull had eventually apologized. The woman said birds had excellent confidence and terrible manners. Her son smiled for the first time since entering. An ordinary table could make room for fear without pretending to treat it.

shoal_e14_public_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_public_07.text: The relative returned while the booking clerk still had time to examine the corrected record. This family's carrier accepted its own journey on the available date. Their care provider retained clinical authority; the transport clerk retained transport authority. Yue's useful work was receiving the right ordinary information and keeping two conversations from being buried under the same pile of papers. She had neither carried a patient nor altered a treatment.

shoal_e14_public_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_public_08.text: At Bo's room, Jin sat beside him and repaired a loose seam on her own coat. He asked whether she was angry about the declined net job. She said she wanted the four copper and had chosen to stay. Both were true. He tried to tell her she should have gone without company arranged. She answered that he could ask her what she wanted instead of deciding her answer after the tide.

shoal_e14_public_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_public_09.text: Their conversation was private and did not become a report at Yue's desk. Bo's prescribed care continued under its existing scope. Jin had missed one actual paid opportunity, not every later client. That distinction mattered when the net owner sent an ordinary note asking about a different repair next week. She was free to consider the new offer, but it did not turn today's declined work into earned money.

shoal_e14_public_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_public_10.text: By the desk's closing bell, both families had their accepted current carrier arrangements. Neither had been required to tell a public story of suffering to receive the ordinary help. Yue filed the receiving extracts under their permitted terms and shut the table at the promised hour. An additional visitor arrived afterward. She directed him to the staffed next interval instead of making her two accepted hours an indefinite personal service.

shoal_e14_public_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_public_11.text: Yue brought Bo an ordinary message that she had finished her offered role. She did not enter without asking. He was tired and preferred no visit that evening, so she left the note with the proper receiving person. The missed conversation remained missed. It was possible that he would want company another day. It was not a reason to claim she had somehow been with him while helping two other households.

shoal_e14_public_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_public_12.text: Jin later thanked the desk for its clear closing time. She had seen public helpers become impossible to find precisely because they promised everyone another hour. She did not thank Yue for the repair payment she had lost. At home she and Bo counted the day's actual costs, argued about a broken kettle, and made their next decisions. Their household remained larger than the part of it the desk had witnessed.

shoal_e14_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_01.text: The harbor's evenings grew warmer. Rain left dark stripes on the piles of salvaged timber, and the public lane smelled of wet hemp where clean rope was hung above muddy wheels. Yue walked home after her paid work at an ordinary pace. Her own elbow still discouraged careless pressure. The port had no shortage of bodies recovering at different speeds, and no bell that announced a single day when all of them would be well.

shoal_e14_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_02.text: On Day Three Hundred Twenty-Five, the second completed week of the receiving appointment paid twenty-five copper for five actual four-hour shifts. Yue checked the dates against her own performed work before putting the money away. The second two-copper restitution installment also arrived under the separate order. It repaid another part of documented clinical expense. It was neither a bonus for enduring violence nor a new right to decide the tool owner's property claim.

shoal_e14_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_03.text: She used received wages for her current room and meals, paying the ordinary agreed rate instead of expecting a charitable bed to extend itself. The innkeeper had begun putting a small pepper dish on her tray because she kept asking for it. One night he forgot. Yue discovered how quickly she could grow attached to a service that had once seemed extravagant simply because it repeated often enough to feel like home.

shoal_e14_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_04.text: Bo's first funded care journey took place on Day Three Hundred Twenty-Six. Its four copper paid the accepted ordinary carrier under the separate eight-copper travel line. Jin accompanied him by her own arrangement. The carrier used its proper support and loading method, and qualified people managed the leg under the current plan. Yue did not make a public spectacle of lifting him. The trip was work that ordinary trained people knew how to perform.

shoal_e14_rejoin_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_05.text: A wheel caught in a shallow rut before they reached the street's smoother stone. The carrier stopped and asked the passenger before adjusting its route. Bo disliked the delay and appreciated the question. Across the lane, a man hurried past carrying fish that could not wait for anyone's dignity. Jin bought two small portions after the appointment because Bo wanted a supper with a smell he associated with working days.

shoal_e14_rejoin_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_06.text: The practitioner reviewed the current leg condition and kept the limits on weight and distance. A journey successfully completed did not prove that heavy hauling was safe. Bo asked for a date when he could stop worrying. The practitioner gave the next actual review date and explained the warning signs that should bring him sooner. Bo looked angry, then wrote them down. Anger could sit beside cooperation without either being false.

shoal_e14_rejoin_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_07.text: On Day Three Hundred Twenty-Seven, four copper supplied the remaining accepted dressings work and materials, completing the ten-copper line with the earlier six. The provider used them for the specified care rather than leaving unopened cloth counted as treatment. The household received the relevant ordinary instructions. Private details stayed with the patient. Yue learned the completed account figure through its permitted public scope, not from searching someone else's intimate record.

shoal_e14_rejoin_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_08.text: The third injured employee returned to an ordinary task sooner than Bo could. He was pleased and embarrassed when Bo congratulated him. He began explaining that his injury had been easier, which Bo already knew. Jin interrupted them both with a request to move a stool. Neither man's recovery needed an apology for differing from the other's. The stool needed moving by someone currently able to do it safely.

shoal_e14_rejoin_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_09.text: The fourth employee's private care update was not offered to Yue. She saw him leaving a doorway with a relative and greeted him without asking for his diagnosis. The town's public curiosity had made some injured people feel as though survival required a daily announcement. She could be interested in a person and still accept an ordinary greeting as the whole conversation he wished to have in the street.

shoal_e14_rejoin_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_10.text: At the receiving room, the two qualified pattern readers disagreed over a partially legible tool drawing. One thought a narrow line marked clearance; the other thought it marked the edge of a broken annotation. Yue received their separate findings instead of smoothing them into agreement. The owner would choose what later work to commission. A doubtful drawing was useful precisely because the missing portion remained visible to the people who might rely on it.

shoal_e14_rejoin_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_11.text: A customer brought a broken brass latch and asked whether the fire fund would replace every tool ruined since the alarm. The receiving clerk explained its actual scope, then helped identify the owner and present loss. The man was disappointed. He also had a genuine unrelated broken latch. Rejecting one unsuitable claim did not turn the man into a fraud or make the town's damaged doors less real.

shoal_e14_rejoin_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_12.text: Yue ate her evening bread on the quay wall where ordinary pedestrians were permitted to sit. Below her, small fish gathered under a dripping rope. A heron waited so still that she initially mistook it for a knot in the dark structure. When it struck, one fish vanished and the others scattered. The bird's hunger had its own purpose. It had not appeared to reassure the harbor that every loss served human growth.

shoal_e14_rejoin_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_13.text: On Day Three Hundred Twenty-Nine, Bo attended the second four-copper rehabilitation session. The practitioner measured the permitted movement against the earlier actual observation and adjusted ordinary work within the same clinical scope. Bo had improved in one respect and found another motion harder that morning. He wanted to call the difficult motion failure. The practitioner called it information about today's leg and stopped where the current limit required stopping.

shoal_e14_rejoin_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_14.text: Jin asked to learn an ordinary support task that the practitioner considered suitable for her. She received actual instruction and practiced under supervision before using it at home. Her willingness did not qualify her for every medical role. The task itself was small enough to fit her life, and she could decline another. Bo thanked her with an awkwardness that suggested he would rather have been offering than receiving help.

shoal_e14_rejoin_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_15.text: Afterward he spoke to a former apprentice about sorting fastenings at a table when the current plan permitted it. The apprentice had found other paid work during the closure. He could offer one specific evening, not restore his old attendance for free. Bo accepted the limited offer and said he would pay for actual work from his own remaining shop money if they agreed a task. A damaged business could still owe someone wages.

shoal_e14_rejoin_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_16.text: Jin's next client sent an ordinary request with a deadline she could consider rather than an assumption that her injury-adjacent household made her available at all hours. She asked about the materials and named her price. The client bargained. She bargained back. Their voices grew cheerful as they found a scope both accepted. Yue, passing outside, could hear the work negotiation without knowing the household's private decision afterward.

shoal_e14_rejoin_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_17.text: At the public room, a child asked why recovering adults looked bored. Han Pei answered that recovery often involved waiting for something that no effort could hurry. The child said waiting was easy if there was a game. Han gave him the stack of obsolete blank covers to invent one. By dusk he had designed a harbor board with too many storms and charged no money because nobody yet knew how to win.

shoal_e14_rejoin_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_18.text: Yue tried the game after closing and lost her imaginary cargo to three weather turns in succession. The child accused her of choosing a bad road. She asked whether any road on his board was better. He examined it, frowned, and changed a rule. His first invention was allowed to need repair. The adults helped test a game without letting its impossible storms explain the town's actual fire.

shoal_e14_rejoin_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_19.text: On Day Three Hundred Thirty, the second five-copper restricted-income payment reached Bo under the accepted six-week schedule. Ten of thirty had now been paid. The rest remained future support for actual later dates. He and Jin decided how to use their household money themselves. Yue was not invited to direct each purchase because she had once helped at a table or sat beside a window.

shoal_e14_rejoin_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_rejoin_20.text: A new ordinary notice described possible rooms beyond the crowded quay. It named current landlords, available dates, and prices, but promised neither work nor that moving would please every household. Families would need to compare their own needs and answer for themselves. Jin pinned it where Bo could read it without reaching. They began discussing what mattered more to them: familiar neighbors, a ground-floor entrance, or the shop they still owned.

shoal_e14_evening_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_01.text: The room notice drew different reactions at the packing tables. An older worker wanted fewer stairs but would not leave the woman who watched his grandchildren in the morning. A young couple wanted distance from the quay noise and disliked the proposed road fare. Neither preference was foolish. The available rooms could solve one difficulty while creating another. Yue copied the current routes onto a public sheet and left the households to decide which costs they could carry.

shoal_e14_evening_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_02.text: He Ming disliked the advertisement's word suitable. Suitable for whom, he asked, tapping a room listed above a steep turn in the stairs. The landlord had supplied accurate dimensions and still imagined a single kind of tenant. Han Pei added the actual entrance details after a permitted inspection. Nobody changed the building into an accessible one by improving its description. A clearer notice would help someone refuse it before spending money on the wrong journey.

shoal_e14_evening_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_03.text: The potter came to the receiving room wearing a clean ordinary hand dressing. He needed to send a message to the buyer whose sailing he had missed during the medicine delay. The original appointment was gone. He could ask whether the buyer wanted a later order, but the buyer owed him no new visit. Yue helped him use the message allowance only where its accepted receiving scope applied and left his separate commercial charge with him.

shoal_e14_evening_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_04.text: He had begun making cups again within his current ordinary hand limits. They were smaller and slower than his old daily output. He offered Yue another cup and looked offended when she assumed he meant a gift. She bought it at his stated price after examining the base. This one stood well. He said he had not forgotten how to make a pot merely because one injured week had made everyone tell him to rest.

shoal_e14_evening_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_05.text: Yue carried the new cup home in both ordinary hands, careful of her elbow and of the lane's loose stone. A boy running backward nearly struck her. His friend caught his sleeve before either touched the cup. They apologized, then resumed their chase with the rules altered so no one had to sprint blind into pedestrians. The small intervention was useful. It did not establish a new force task or require Yue to demonstrate a cultivation stage.

shoal_e14_evening_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_06.text: At supper the innkeeper announced a communal fish stew funded by the customers who actually ordered portions. It was neither a relief feast charged to the care deposit nor evidence that all households could now afford supper there. Yue paid her share. One guest wanted more pepper, another less salt, and the cook said both could season their own bowls after he had finished feeding the people whose orders were accepted.

shoal_e14_evening_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_07.text: Song Mei joined the table after her own paid rehearsal. She had rented a room for her current stay from received performance income and existing savings. The fire had not made every artist a relief worker. She asked Yue whether the harbor now knew her as a witness, a receiving clerk, or an imaginary woman standing inside flames. Yue said different people appeared to prefer different versions. Song said the versions could send their own supper money.

shoal_e14_evening_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_08.text: The joke drew a laugh from a rigger who had actually been at the ordinary crew line. He described the foreman's most frequent instruction: step back from the rope. The public stories preferred charges forward. He wanted one song in which a person obeyed and therefore remained useful afterward. Song considered it as an artistic suggestion, not an order. She said a chorus about sensible feet might have possibilities if the feet also had rhythm.

shoal_e14_evening_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_09.text: A traveler from the southern causeway carried news of a bridge repaired on its actual inspection date. He did not know whether the next rain would leave it open. The table asked about prices, family visits, and which road inn still served fresh vegetables. News moved at the pace of people who had actually traveled. Nobody at the meal possessed a view of every road between the harbor and the distant mine.

shoal_e14_evening_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_10.text: Bo could not attend that supper under his current transport and fatigue plan. Jin brought a paid portion home because he wanted it and the price fit their actual household decision. She did not describe the meal as a substitute for going out. He missed the noise and other people's quarrels. She told him the cook's argument about salt anyway, and he laughed at the part she thought he would like.

shoal_e14_evening_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_11.text: Later Jin asked whether a future ground-floor room would leave them too far from her best net clients. Bo suggested keeping the shop as a daytime place if the separate rents were affordable. She asked him to calculate the cost instead of falling in love with an arrangement before knowing its price. He found the notebook. Their disagreement was practical, intimate, and unfinished. It did not need Yue to select an answer for them.

shoal_e14_evening_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_12.text: Across town, one of the two families whose journey was discussed at the auxiliary desk received a current carrier message. The particular booking history belonged to that family and its own accepted receiving. Yue saw only that the regular desk had completed its ordinary message delivery. She did not infer which path another household had followed from a sealed envelope crossing the room. The desk had real work beyond her short offered interval.

shoal_e14_evening_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_13.text: Han Pei closed the day's books before darkness made the figures harder to read. A candle could extend office hours, but someone still had to pay for fuel and for the person holding the office open. He preferred to keep the advertised ordinary hours and give urgent defined work its own accepted staffing. Yue helped return the public weights to their shelf. Neither mistook tidying the room for an additional paid shift.

shoal_e14_evening_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_14.text: Outside, the breeze shifted and carried a faint burned smell from the closed shed ground. Some neighbors had grown used to it; others still woke when smoke from an ordinary kitchen reached their beds. The town was changing its work without changing all its memories at the same speed. Yue walked past the marked boundary and saw fresh grass pushing through a strip of ground untouched by the inspection trench.

shoal_e14_evening_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_15.text: She had no great revelation beside the grass. Her feet hurt from the day's ordinary walking, and she wanted sleep. Recovery had produced useful hours, tedious hours, and hours that she understood only when another person explained why they mattered. Before bed she wrote her current commitments in plain dates: paid receiving, her own clinical limits, and no promised road job yet. The empty space after them remained available for a future decision.

shoal_e14_evening_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_16.text: The harbor clock struck from a tower that ordinary maintenance workers had kept running throughout the fire. One gear sounded rougher than it used to, but the clock's keeper had an accepted repair day and a replacement part actually ordered. Yue heard the hour through her open window. The town had many such modest continuities. They were work by specific people, not a hidden power holding everything safe while others suffered.

shoal_e14_evening_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_17.text: In the morning, Han Pei posted the room information beside the current wage notices. He wrote that visits required the landlords' accepted times and that each household should ask about its own entrance and lease. People began making plans before the ink fully dried. A woman who had wanted the same block for years now found she wanted a different town. Her husband stared at her, then asked what road she had in mind.

shoal_e14_evening_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_18.text: Yue watched the husband listening. He did not agree immediately. Their grandchildren lived near the quay, and he had made promises about helping with them. The woman said she had made promises too and wanted those included in the account. They took the notice away together. Nobody at the board heard what they decided afterward. A public housing list could begin a private argument, but its clerk did not own the ending of that argument or the people who carried the paper home to discuss it.

shoal_e14_evening_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e14_evening_19.text: At the next receiving shift, Yue opened the shutters before the first customer arrived. She set out three ordinary chairs so a visitor did not have to stand through a long question. The chairs had not cured Bo's leg or restored any burned stock. They made one working room easier to use. Outside, the harbor began another day of boats, bargaining, appointments, and unfinished household choices. Some brought losses she could only acknowledge. She listened for the first knock and let the person entering tell her what help was wanted that morning.
